# Balanced 3x2 factorial ANOVA
# Factor A: 3 levels (numerator df = 2)
# Factor B: 2 levels
# Full interaction model with common variance
# Partial eta-squared for Factor A main effect = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80

# Input parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
df_numerator <- 2  # Factor A has 3 levels, so df = 3-1 = 2

# For a balanced 3x2 design with n participants per cell:
# - Total N = 6n
# - Error df = Total N - (number of cell means) = 6n - 6
# - This assumes a full factorial model with main effects and interaction

# Convert partial eta-squared to noncentrality parameter lambda
# Formula: partial_eta_sq = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# Solving for lambda: lambda = partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)

# Function to calculate power for given n per cell
calculate_power <- function(n_per_cell) {
  total_N <- 6 * n_per_cell
  df_error <- total_N - 6  # 6 cells in the design
  
  # Calculate noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_error) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F-value at alpha = 0.05
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit | H1 is true, lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(n_per_cell = n_per_cell, 
             total_N = total_N,
             df_error = df_error, 
             lambda = lambda, 
             f_crit = f_crit,
             power = power))
}

# Search for minimum n that gives power >= 0.80
# Start with a reasonable range
n_candidates <- 1:100

results <- lapply(n_candidates, calculate_power)
powers <- sapply(results, function(x) x$power)

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- n_candidates[min_idx]

# Verify the solution and examine neighboring values
cat("=== Sample Size Calculation for Factorial ANOVA ===\n")
cat("Design: 3-level Factor A × 2-level Factor B (balanced, all cells independent)\n")
cat("Model: Full interaction model with common variance\n")
cat("Effect: Main effect of Factor A (numerator df = 2)\n")
cat("Partial eta-squared = ", partial_eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Alpha = ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target Power = ", target_power, "\n\n")

# Show results for n = min_n - 1, min_n, min_n + 1
check_indices <- (min_n - 1):(min_n + 1)
for (i in check_indices) {
  res <- calculate_power(i)
  cat(sprintf("n per cell = %d | Total N = %d | df_error = %d | lambda = %.4f | Power = %.4f\n",
              res$n_per_cell, res$total_N, res$df_error, res$lambda, res$power))
}

cat("\n=== MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE ===\n")
res_min <- calculate_power(min_n)
cat(sprintf("Minimum n per cell = %d\n", min_n))
cat(sprintf("Total participants N = %d\n", res_min$total_N))
cat(sprintf("Error degrees of freedom = %d\n", res_min$df_error))
cat(sprintf("Noncentrality parameter λ = %.4f\n", res_min$lambda))
cat(sprintf("Critical F-value at α=0.05 = %.4f\n", res_min$f_crit))
cat(sprintf("Achieved Power = %.6f\n", res_min$power))

# Also check the preceding design
res_prev <- calculate_power(min_n - 1)
cat("\n=== POWER AT PRECEDING DESIGN ===\n")
cat(sprintf("n per cell = %d | Power = %.6f\n", min_n - 1, res_prev$power))

# Return the minimum sample size
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_cell"),
      list(metric = "total_participants", value = res_min$total_N, unit = "count"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = res_min$power, unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = res_prev$power, unit = "proportion")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

# Balanced 3×2 factorial ANOVA for main effect of Factor A
# Test: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ (numerator df = 2)
# Effect size: partial η² = 0.06

library(stats)

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
df_numerator <- 2  # 3 levels - 1

# Design structure verification:
# - 3-level Factor A × 2-level Factor B
# - n participants per cell
# - Total N = 3 × 2 × n = 6n
# - Cells (treatment combinations): A₁B₁, A₁B₂, A₂B₁, A₂B₂, A₃B₁, A₃B₂ (6 cells)
# - Full interaction model parameters: 1 (intercept) + 2 (Factor A main) + 1 (Factor B main) + 2 (A×B interaction) = 6 parameters
# - Error df = 6n - 6 (total observations minus total parameters estimated)

cat("=== DESIGN SPECIFICATION VERIFICATION ===\n")
cat("Factorial structure: 3 (Factor A) × 2 (Factor B)\n")
cat("Number of cells: 6\n")
cat("Model: Full factorial with main effects and interaction\n")
cat("Cell means to estimate: 6\n")
cat("Error df formula: 6n - 6 (where n = participants per cell)\n\n")

# Function to compute power for a given n per cell
compute_power_factorial <- function(n_cell) {
  N_total <- 6 * n_cell
  df_error <- N_total - 6  # 6 parameters in full model
  
  # Convert partial eta-squared to noncentrality parameter
  # Relationship: η²_p = λ / (λ + df_error)
  # Solving for λ: λ = η²_p × df_error / (1 - η²_p)
  
  if (partial_eta_sq >= 1) {
    return(NA)
  }
  
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_error) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F-value at α = 0.05 with df₁=2, df₂=df_error
  f_critical <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error)
  
  # Power under noncentral F-distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_critical, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(
    n_cell = n_cell,
    N_total = N_total,
    df_error = df_error,
    lambda = lambda,
    f_critical = f_critical,
    power = power
  ))
}

# Balanced 3x2 factorial ANOVA
# Factor A: 3 levels (numerator df = 2)
# Factor B: 2 levels
# Full interaction model with common variance
# Partial eta-squared for Factor A main effect = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80

# Input parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
df_numerator <- 2  # Factor A has 3 levels, so df = 3-1 = 2

# For a balanced 3x2 design with n participants per cell:
# - Total N = 6n
# - Error df = Total N - (number of cell means) = 6n - 6
# - This assumes a full factorial model with main effects and interaction

# Convert partial eta-squared to noncentrality parameter lambda
# Formula: partial_eta_sq = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# Solving for lambda: lambda = partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)

# Function to calculate power for given n per cell
calculate_power <- function(n_per_cell) {
  total_N <- 6 * n_per_cell
  df_error <- total_N - 6  # 6 cells in the design
  
  # Calculate noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_error) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F-value at alpha = 0.05
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit | H1 is true, lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(n_per_cell = n_per_cell, 
             total_N = total_N,
             df_error = df_error, 
             lambda = lambda, 
             f_crit = f_crit,
             power = power))
}

# Search for minimum n that gives power >= 0.80
# Start with a reasonable range
n_candidates <- 1:100

results <- lapply(n_candidates, calculate_power)
powers <- sapply(results, function(x) x$power)

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- n_candidates[min_idx]

# Verify the solution and examine neighboring values
cat("=== Sample Size Calculation for Factorial ANOVA ===\n")
cat("Design: 3-level Factor A × 2-level Factor B (balanced, all cells independent)\n")
cat("Model: Full interaction model with common variance\n")
cat("Effect: Main effect of Factor A (numerator df = 2)\n")
cat("Partial eta-squared = ", partial_eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Alpha = ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target Power = ", target_power, "\n\n")

# Show results for n = min_n - 1, min_n, min_n + 1
check_indices <- (min_n - 1):(min_n + 1)
for (i in check_indices) {
  res <- calculate_power(i)
  cat(sprintf("n per cell = %d | Total N = %d | df_error = %d | lambda = %.4f | Power = %.4f\n",
              res$n_per_cell, res$total_N, res$df_error, res$lambda, res$power))
}

cat("\n=== MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE ===\n")
res_min <- calculate_power(min_n)
cat(sprintf("Minimum n per cell = %d\n", min_n))
cat(sprintf("Total participants N = %d\n", res_min$total_N))
cat(sprintf("Error degrees of freedom = %d\n", res_min$df_error))
cat(sprintf("Noncentrality parameter λ = %.4f\n", res_min$lambda))
cat(sprintf("Critical F-value at α=0.05 = %.4f\n", res_min$f_crit))
cat(sprintf("Achieved Power = %.6f\n", res_min$power))

cat("\n=== POWER AT PRECEDING DESIGN ===\n")

# - 3-level Factor A × 2-level Factor B

# - Cells (treatment combinations): A₁B₁, A₁B₂, A₂B₁, A₂B₂, A₃B₁, A₃B₂ (6 cells)
# - Full interaction model parameters: 1 (intercept) + 2 (Factor A main) + 1 (Factor B main) + 2 (A×B interaction) = 6 parameters
# - Error df = 6n - 6 (total observations minus total parameters estimated)

cat("=== DESIGN SPECIFICATION VERIFICATION ===\n")
cat("Factorial structure: 3 (Factor A) × 2 (Factor B)\n")
cat("Number of cells: 6\n")
cat("Model: Full factorial with main effects and interaction\n")
cat("Cell means to estimate: 6\n")
cat("Error df formula: 6n - 6 (where n = participants per cell)\n\n")

# Function to compute power for a given n per cell
compute_power_factorial <- function(n_cell) {
  N_total <- 6 * n_cell
  df_error <- N_total - 6  # 6 parameters in full model
  
  # Convert partial eta-squared to noncentrality parameter
  # Relationship: η²_p = λ / (λ + df_error)
  # Solving for λ: λ = η²_p × df_error / (1 - η²_p)
  
  if (partial_eta_sq >= 1) {
    return(NA)
  }
  
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_error) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F-value at α = 0.05 with df₁=2, df₂=df_error
  f_critical <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error)
  
  # Power under noncentral F-distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_critical, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(
    n_cell = n_cell,
    N_total = N_total,
    df_error = df_error,
    lambda = lambda,
    f_critical = f_critical,
    power = power
  ))
}

calculate_power <- function(n_per_cell) {

  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit | H1 is true, lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error, ncp = lambda)
